requirement:
A named item's `name_span` is `Some` with the span to highlight for its name
in the original source snapshot. The highlighted text may differ from the
name in the selector. Use `selector` to address the item. The file root and
anonymous items have `name_span` set to `None`. `OutlineItem::new` starts with
`None`. Language providers use `with_name_span` to set the highlight within
the item’s own span.
rationale:
Obligations and coverage:

1. Named items have `name_span` = Some with the highlight span in the original source, which may differ from the selector name. `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[rust_name_spans_highlight_spelling_in_the_original_source]` asserts the source text of each Rust span: `Trait for Wrapper<T>` against selector `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`, `café`, `extern` and `"C"` against selector `extern[Rust]`. `fn[language_name_spans_retain_original_bytes_when_selectors_are_normalized]` does the same for Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown. It uses spacing and quoting that selector normalization would alter, such as `screen   and (color)`, `'c/d'` and `Café   title`. The duplicate TS names also assert distinct spans.

2. The file root and anonymous items have `None`. Both multi-language tests assert `items[0].name_span == None`. Anonymous Rust `use` items, Markdown directive items and plain text items are asserted `None`. In `src/outline/contents.rs#mod[tests]/fn[provider_name_spans_match_selector_kind_and_item_boundaries]`, a hash-selector (anonymous) item is valid only with `None`. A named item with `None` is rejected.

3. `OutlineItem::new` starts with `None`. `fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` asserts `item.name_span == None` right after `new`.

4. `with_name_span` sets the highlight within the item's own span. The constructor test sets `Span(7,8)` inside the item span `(2,12)` and asserts it is preserved after cloning. The provider-boundary test checks that a span within the item and on char boundaries is valid. It rejects reversed spans, spans starting before the item or ending after it, and a span splitting the multibyte `é`.

These tests have {test} markers for the requirement and have meaningful assertions. I found no unmarked relevant test and no unacknowledged gap.
